items.entity: L-shaped design domain (arm width / size of the removed corner square)
items.description: Sec. 4 'Example designs' and the Fig. 4 caption only say 'classic L-shaped bracket' from the out-of-distribution set. Sec. 3.1 'Dataset' says those instances use randomly drawn parameters. No arm width, cut-out size or aspect parameter is reported, so the geometry is visible only in Fig. 4. The lengths of the clamped face and the loaded face also follow from it.
readings: arm width 0.4·L (≈26 of 64 elements), 0.6L × 0.6L corner removed (classic L-bracket proportions)
arm width 0.3·L (≈19 elements), 0.7L × 0.7L corner removed
arm width 0.2·L (≈13 elements), 0.8L × 0.8L corner removed
arm width 0.5·L (32 elements), 0.5L × 0.5L corner removed

items.entity: void (cut-out) corner of the L, modelled as passive void elements in the square grid
items.description: The text never says which corner of the square bounding box is void, or that it must be a passive (rho = 0, E = Emin) region on the structured grid. The orientation is only implied by 'classic', 'clamped support along the top edge' and 'load applied at the right edge' in the Fig. 4 caption; otherwise it is shown only in the figure.
readings: upper-right corner void: vertical arm on the left clamped on its top face, horizontal arm along the bottom loaded at its right tip (classic)
lower-left corner void (L rotated 180°): arm along the full top edge is clamped, and the arm along the right edge carries the load at its lower end

items.description: The FE mesh for this example is never stated. Sec. 3.1 says designs are 'represented as grayscale images of fixed resolution (64x64)' and gives the filter radius in pixels. The fracture section resizes the LBAE output to fit a 64x128-element mesh, which implies 64x64 elements are native. However, the source problems of [19] are defined at other resolutions, so a square 64x64 element grid is implied, not stated.
readings: 64 × 64 square bilinear elements on a square bounding box, one element per pixel (filter radius = 2 elements)
finer square grid (e.g. 128 × 128) with filter radius 2 elements, design down-sampled to 64 × 64 afterwards

items.entity: clamped support on the top edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption says only 'clamped support along the top edge'. The clamped length equals the unknown arm width (figure only). The text does not say whether only the top face of the arm is fixed or the whole top row of grid nodes, including nodes above the void corner.
readings: fix u_x and u_y at all nodes of the vertical arm's top face (outer corner to re-entrant corner)
fix all nodes of the full top edge of the square grid, including nodes over the void corner (practically equivalent if the corner is passive void)

items.entity: downward point load on the right edge
items.description: The Fig. 4 caption gives only 'a downward point load applied at the right edge'. It does not say where on the right end face of the horizontal arm the load sits, and the height of that face is itself unknown. The exact node is shown only in Fig. 4.
readings: mid-height of the horizontal arm's right end face (0.5 × arm width above the bottom edge)
upper corner of the right end face (height = arm width, top surface of the arm)
bottom-right corner node of the domain

items.description: No force magnitude is given anywhere for this example. Sec. 3.1 and Sec. 3.2 give only E0 = 1.0, Emin = 1e-9 and nu = 0.3.
readings: F = 1 (unit load, consistent with the normalised E0 = 1)
any other magnitude (e.g. F = 100), which only rescales compliance

items.entity: prescribed volume fraction V0 of the L-bracket instance
items.description: V0 for the Fig. 4 problem is not reported. Out-of-distribution parameters were 'drawn at random from a uniform distribution' (Sec. 3.1 'Dataset') with no stated range. Only the training-set range [0.12, 0.5] is given.

items.entity: reference area for V0 (L region vs full square)
items.description: Eq. (2) in Sec. 3.2 imposes the integral of rho over 'the design domain Omega' = V0. For an L-bracket on a square grid with a masked corner, the text does not say whether Omega is the L-shaped region or the whole square. With a 0.6L cut-out, the available material differs by a factor of 0.64 between the two readings.
readings: V0 is a fraction of the L-shaped (non-void) region only
V0 is a fraction of the full square grid, with the void corner counted as zero density

items.description: Sec. 3.1 says the simulations follow the 88-line code with E0 = 1.0, Emin = 1e-9 and nu = 0.3. The penalty exponent is a user input in that code and is never given, and no continuation scheme is mentioned.
readings: p = 3 (fixed)
p increased by continuation, e.g. 1 -> 3
another fixed value, e.g. p = 4

items.entity: cone density filter (radius 2 px) next to the void corner
items.description: Sec. 3.1 and Sec. 3.2 specify a standard cone filter of radius 2 pixels but not how it treats the passive void corner. If void elements are included in filter neighbourhoods, densities along the re-entrant edges are softened; a mask-aware filter avoids this.
readings: mask-aware filter: void elements excluded and weights renormalised over the L region
plain 88-line density filter over the full square grid, with void elements reset to 0 after filtering

items.entity: volume-constraint handling / MMA settings for the reference (ground-truth) solve
items.description: Sec. 3.1 states only 'MMA ... with the default hyperparameter settings', 200 iterations and an 88-line-style set-up. The sigmoid/bisection volume mapping of Eq. (2) is described for the neural-network outputs. It is unclear whether the MMA reference used that mapping or an explicit constraint on filtered densities. Move-limit and asymptote defaults depend on which MMA implementation is used.
readings: MMA on element densities with an explicit volume constraint on filtered (physical) densities, Svanberg default parameters, 200 iterations
MMA on unconstrained logits mapped by the sigmoid with bisection-enforced mean (Eq. 2) before the cone filter (Hoyer et al. style), 200 iterations

items.entity: thresholding for the binary (thresholded) designs reported in Fig. 4
items.description: Sec. 3.2 'Performance metrics' only cites 'the simplest strategy from [66]'. The heat-conduction section describes rounding to 0/1 'while preserving the volume fraction', but the rule used for Fig. 4 is not stated. It affects only the post-processed binary design and its compliance, not the optimised grayscale design.
readings: volume-preserving threshold: the V0·N densest elements set to 1, the rest to 0
fixed cut-off at rho = 0.5

locator: Sec. 4 'Example designs', Fig. 4 (the first problem instance shown with a design)
